subject: Indemnity tiering and evidence responsibility for Order Form
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@cloudify.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@cloudify.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity tiering and evidence responsibility for Order Form

Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attaching our latest redline of the Order Form (Cloudify_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf) and an evidence checklist that we use for third‑party infringement inquiries (indemnity_evidence_checklist.xlsx). A few open items that we need to converge on before we can get procurement signoff: 

- Tiering: Cloudify has asked to limit the right to defend to claims arising from their direct use and seek a higher cap for third‑party IP. We proposed a split (customer indemnity for direct customer content, Redwood to defend for model‑generated infringement) — please confirm whether you can live with the proposed 50/50 split for defense costs above the self‑insured retention.
- Escrow/escrow triggers: Cloudify wants escrow activation on any claim exceeding $250k. Our standard is $500k. Need procurement position.
- Evidence flow & timelines: We propose 5 business days to produce technical evidence and 10 business days for litigation hold paperwork. Cloudify counsel requested tighter windows; see the checklist.

Action items:
- Elena / Rajiv: flag the terms you cannot accept and suggest alternative language by Tue EOD PT.
- Kimberly: can you confirm the legal fallback language (preserve defense control but allow reimbursement) and whether we can accept the $250k trigger if Cloudify takes a higher insurance contribution?
- Ben: ops estimate of evidence collection (SLA for logs, model weights, prompt captures) — can we meet 5 business days?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if that helps.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Legal, Contracts

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@cloudify.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Indemnity tiering and evidence responsibility for Order Form

Sergio —

Quick reply from Cloudify Legal after internal review. High level: we appreciate the split but cannot accept anything that effectively shifts primary defense responsibility for third‑party patent claims to the vendor for model outputs. Two concrete asks:

1) Defense control: Cloudify insists on right to assume defense for third‑party claims that allege use of Cloudify’s environment or customer prompts (i.e., claims tied to how the customer used the model). We can propose a carveout for clear vendor‑owned training data infringement.
2) Escrow trigger: we can move the trigger to $400k if Redwood accepts a mutual notice period extension to 15 business days for evidence requests.

We will propose redline text for both items tomorrow. Also, need to ensure evidence delivery: Cloudify can commit to producing prompt logs and job metadata within 7 business days but cannot provide model weights or internal model artifacts.

— Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
Senior Counsel, Cloudify Corp
rajiv.patel@cloudify.com

Subject: Fwd: Indemnity tiering and evidence responsibility for Order Form

Sergio / Ben —

Forwarding Rajiv's reply. My legal take: we should stick to defense control for vendor‑owned model IP and accept Cloudify's assumption for customer usage claims with a narrowly drawn definition. Proposed language bullets below for internal negotiation with procurement: 

- Definition: "Vendor Model IP" = model architecture, weights, and vendor training data; "Customer Use Claims" = claims arising from customer‑provided prompts, instructions, or configuration of the model instance.
- Defense handover: Redwood will retain right to defend Vendor Model IP claims; Cloudify may assume defense of Customer Use Claims but Redwood reserves reimbursement rights for (i) settlements caused by failure to follow Redwood's published safeguards, and (ii) any covered cost allocations inconsistent with agreed insurance waterfall.
- Escrow/trigger: accept $400k if Cloudify agrees to a 12 business day accelerated evidence covenant (we can compress to 12 instead of 15 if they accept a mutual on‑site data access review).

Ben — can you confirm ops availability for 12 business days for the logs/metadata pull? If not, we should counter with $500k trigger and 10 business days.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Indemnity tiering and evidence responsibility for Order Form

Kimberly / Sergio —

Ops update: we can produce prompt logs, run history, and invocation metadata within 10 business days from notice during normal operating load. 12 business days is achievable if we prioritize the request and allocate a small incident team (adds minor cost). We cannot provide model weights or training dataset exports (technical/legal limitation).

Given that, I'm comfortable recommending we accept the $400k trigger with a 12 business day evidence SLA and the mutual on‑site review language. I'll note the additional ops effort in the procurement SOW as a line item (est. one FTE week for triage & export coordination).

If Cloudify confirms the defense carveout language for Vendor Model IP, we can move to final redline and DocuSign.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
